product: Moulded fruit-shaped frozen sorbet — sorbet cast in the exact silhouette of the real fruit (strawberry, apricot, lemon, fig, blackberry), airbrushed to fruit colour, usually inside a thin cracking shell. Arabic working name for the deck: «فَاكِهَةٌ مُجَمَّدَة» / "Frozen Fruit". Industry names in the four markets that matter: 3D Fruit Ice Cream (US/Japan), 프로즌 소르베 / Frozen Sorbet (Korea), 3Dフルーツアイス (Japan), 水果造型冰淇淋 / 福芒·桃气·柠夏 (China), Pops / Mix Pops (Qatar & GCC).
origin:
FOUR SEPARATE LINEAGES CONVERGE — the deck should tell it as a line that starts in the Arab world, passes through Sicily and Paris, and comes back.

1) SICILY, 12th CENTURY — «فاكهة المارتورانا» (frutta martorana). The oldest documented European tradition of sculpting and painting sweets into hyper-realistic fruit. Made by the Benedictine nuns of the convent beside the church of Santa Maria dell'Ammiraglio in Palermo, nicknamed "La Martorana." The church was erected in 1143 by Giorgio d'Antiochia (George of Antioch), admiral to Roger II of Sicily; in 1193 the noblewoman Eloisia Martorana had the Benedictine monastery built next to it. The legend: an archbishop announced a visit in early November, the trees in the cloister were bare, so the nuns hung vivid marzipan replicas of fruit on the branches. He was pleased; they kept making them and began selling them to parishioners. THE HOOK FOR AN ARAB BRAND: the marzipan itself — almonds and sugar — arrived in Sicily in the 9th century with the Arab conquest of the island. The technique of moulding sugar-and-almond into fruit is Arab in origin and Sicilian only in expression. SHABIM is not borrowing a European idea; it is repatriating one. (Sources: en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Frutta_martorana; Atlas Obscura / Gastro Obscura; Forbes, Rebecca Hughes, 25 Oct 2022; Katie Parla; Visit Sicily; enjoysicilia.it. Confidence: HIGH on the 1143/1193/9th-century framing, MEDIUM on the archbishop legend, which every source presents as legend.)

2) PARIS, 2010s — CÉDRIC GROLET, the technical template. Executive pastry chef at Le Meurice. He moulds a thin white-chocolate shell and airbrushes it to replicate lemons, apples, figs and hazelnuts, filling it with a compote and confit of the fruit it imitates. Opened his first pastry shop inside Le Meurice in March 2018; named World's Best Pastry Chef 2018 at the World's 50 Best Restaurants awards; passed 1 million Instagram followers by July 2018 (Malay Mail, 10 Jul 2018) and now sits near 10 million. Every frozen fruit-shaped product on the market today is running Grolet's exact construction — moulded shell, airbrushed gradient, fruit interior — at a lower price point. (Sources: en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cédric_Grolet; malaymail.com 10 Jul 2018, 03 Apr 2019, 19 Oct 2019; sites.rutgers.edu French magazine; worldcrunch.com on the French trompe-l'œil craze.)

3) SOUTH AFRICA — ISLAND WAY SORBET, the "real shell" ancestor. Sorbet served inside the actual hollowed fruit rather than a mould. Manufactured by Dynamic Food (South Africa); Frozen Innovations is the Australia/NZ distributor; islandway.co.za, islandway.com and islandway.me run the regional storefronts, including a Middle East site. Their own stated reason for the whole business model: shells are hand-cut, hand-scooped and hand-filled "because the shapes and sizes that grow in nature's orchards can't be handled by machines." That sentence is the entire economic argument of the category. WARNING FOR THE DECK: a widely-copied blog (migatrendz.com) claims Island Way was founded in 1995 in Durban by brothers "Paul and Leslie Bernardini." I could not corroborate this against any company or primary source and it reads as AI-generated SEO filler. DO NOT put that founder claim on a slide.

4) CHINA — where it actually became a manufactured product, and the real "inventor" of this SKU. Two named factories:
   • 红旗 (Hong Qi / "Red Flag") — 红旗冷饮总厂, founded 1992 in Jilin City, Jilin Province. Its bars 福芒 (Fumang, "Propitious Mango"), 桃气 (peach) and 柠夏 (lemon) are the products the English-speaking internet knows as "Propitious Mango ice cream." English Wikipedia carries a standalone article: mango-flavoured ice cream on a wooden stick, thin crunchy white-chocolate coating, made by Hong Qi, "became viral in 2024."
   • 启航食品 / Qi Hang Food Co., Ltd — named in Japanese trade press as the Chinese manufacturer behind the "3D Fruit Ice" now sold at 7-Eleven Japan.
   • Aiko Garden — Chinese brand behind the "Fruit Bucket" pint and the Costco US 4-bar pack.
   • The automation moat is explicitly Chinese: shapesnow.com markets itself as "China Only Full Automated 3D Ice Cream Manufacturer." Everyone outside China is doing this by hand.

VERDICT ON "WHO INVENTED IT": nobody invented the fruit-shaped frozen sorbet in one stroke. Sicilian nuns invented the fruit trompe-l'œil (12th c., on Arab technique); Cédric Grolet invented the modern moulded-shell-plus-airbrush construction (Paris, mid-2010s); Hong Qi in Jilin turned it into a wrapped industrial bar (viral 2024); Mystical in Doha turned it into a fresh gelato-filled Gulf product (2024–25).

— 2026: US MASS RETAIL, AND PRICE COMPRESSION —
• 2026 — Costco US stocks Aiko Garden 3D Fruit Ice Cream Variety Pack, item #2063111, 4 bars × 3.0 oz (75g), $7.39 — i.e. $1.85 a bar. Six-packs of peach and mango reported at $11.69. (PR-sourced: treat the adjectives as marketing, the Costco roadshow fact as real.)
• 08 Aug 2026 — two weeks ago — @ayosafespace still posting Costco fruit-sorbet reviews (7671754335658741023). The category is live this month.

— IS IT RISING OR HAS IT PEAKED? —
MY CALL: geographically staggered. The IMPORTED INDUSTRIAL BAR has peaked; the FRESH, LOCALLY-MADE version has not. Evidence for the peak of the industrial version: Qatar went cloud-kitchen → Monoprix/Carrefour national distribution by Jan 2025; Korea hit 1M units/month by Sept 2025 and a Korean TikTok search page already exists for «과일 모양 아이스크림 망고 단종» ("fruit-shaped ice cream mango — discontinued"), i.e. SKU churn; Japan is a late entrant (Dec 2025); and by 2026 Costco is selling it at $1.85/bar with press framing it as "now affordable." Mass retail plus price compression is the standard end-of-novelty signature — exactly the arc Dubai chocolate ran. Evidence it is NOT over: Costco listings and reviews are still landing in August 2026; the Gulf premium tier (Mystical at 35 QAR ≈ $9.60 a box, Sharjah tubs at AED 75) has not been price-compressed at all; and Iraq is essentially unserved — the only Baghdad fruit ice cream I could find is loose product at Aswaq Center Al-Jamiaa at 1,000 IQD (~$0.76) a piece, i.e. a market with no premium player in it. CAVEAT: I could not pull Google Trends (search budget exhausted), so this is inference from distribution and pricing milestones, not from a trend curve. Label it as judgement on the slide.

STRATEGIC READ FOR SHABIM: do not enter as the import. Enter where Mystical entered — fresh, made in market, gelato/sorbet at real fruit density, Arabic-named, with an orchard fruit set (fig, apricot, blackberry, lemon) that no Chinese factory makes. Every competitor on earth is selling the same five Chinese fruits: mango, peach, grape, strawberry, lemon. Fig and apricot are unclaimed.

hard_to_copy:
SIX STRUCTURAL BARRIERS, ordered by how defensible they actually are.

1) THE MOULD IS THE PRODUCT, AND THE GOOD MOULDS ARE A CHOKEPOINT. The difference between "looks like a fruit" and "looks like a toy" is one engineering detail. Silikomart's professional 3Design / «Frutta 3D» line builds a revolutionary internal border into each cavity that curves the base of the casting inward — so a half-mould reads as a WHOLE fruit rather than a sliced hemisphere. That detail is patented design work by an Italian manufacturer, sold as a 7-mould realistic-fruit kit at €145 RRP (€110.66 on sale) and single moulds around €18. The Amazon alternative is a 3-cavity tray for a few dollars — and it is instantly visible in the finished product from a metre away. A copycat in Baghdad will buy the cheap tray, and the difference will be legible in every photo. Platinum silicone rated −60°C to +230°C is also what lets you go mould → blast freezer without warping; cheap silicone does not survive that cycle.

2) AIRBRUSHED COCOA BUTTER IS A TRAINED HAND, NOT A RECIPE. Cédric Grolet's construction — a 1–2mm shell, then a two-tone airbrushed gradient — needs a compressor, tempered coloured cocoa butter, and someone who can lay the blush on an apricot so it reads as sun-exposure rather than paint. That is skilled labour per unit, and it does not scale by hiring faster. It is the single hardest thing in the product to teach and the easiest thing for a customer to judge.

3) THE AUTOMATION MOAT IS CHINESE — SO DON'T FIGHT ON THAT AXIS. shapesnow.com openly brands itself "China Only Full Automated 3D Ice Cream Manufacturer." Hong Qi has been running cold-dessert lines in Jilin since 1992. They land four bars at Costco for $7.39 — $1.85 a bar. No Gulf or Iraqi operation will beat that on cost, ever. The defensible position is the exact opposite spec: fresh, made in market, high fruit load, no palm-oil compound coating — a product the import PHYSICALLY CANNOT match, because the import has to survive a 45-day sea container and therefore needs stabilisers, compound coating and lower fruit solids. The Costco bar's coating is literally described in US coverage as a "chocolate-flavoured palm oil coating." That is the gap to sell into.

4) COLD CHAIN IS THE REAL BARRIER IN IRAQ AND THE GULF, AND IT IS BRUTAL. A moulded fruit is a thin-walled object with a very high surface-to-volume ratio — the sculpted detail (the fig's neck, the blackberry's drupelets, the strawberry's seed pits) sits at the thinnest, most heat-vulnerable part of the casting. One heat-shock cycle rounds every edge and blooms the shell white. In a Baghdad summer, any operator without an unbroken −18°C chain from mould to hand delivers a blurred, sweating, chalk-dusted object that photographs badly — which kills the only marketing channel this category has. This is not a slogan; it is an operational filter that eliminates most would-be copycats before they open.

5) REAL FRUIT AT REAL DENSITY IS A SOURCING RELATIONSHIP, NOT A RECIPE. The Korean copy for GS25's strawberry is the exact promise: "the fresh tartness of real strawberry flesh, a rich texture as if the fruit had been ground straight in," zero artificial colouring. To deliver that you need contracted fruit at peak ripeness, and you need to freeze it as purée within hours. Island Way's own explanation of why they hand-cut every shell is the same economics stated from the other side: "the shapes and sizes that grow in nature's orchards can't be handled by machines." Handwork and fruit contracts are both slow to build and slow to copy.

6) THE FLAVOUR SET IS UNCLAIMED — AND THAT IS THE CHEAPEST MOAT AVAILABLE. Every single competitor on earth sells the same five Chinese fruits: mango, peach, grape, strawberry, lemon. Hong Qi: mango/peach/lemon. Aiko Garden: mango/grape/peach/strawberry (+ banana, blueberry in the bucket). GS25: mango/peach/lemon/strawberry. Japan 7-Eleven: mango/strawberry/lemon/peach/grape. Mystical Qatar is the only one that broke the set, and it did so with LOZ (لوز) and pistachio kunafa — and it is the only brand of the group that owns a country. SHABIM's brief already names FIG, APRICOT and BLACKBERRY. Nobody makes those. تين and مشمش are Levantine/Iraqi orchard fruit with an emotional register that mango does not have in Baghdad, and a Chinese factory will not tool a mould for a market it doesn't serve. Combined with an Arabic brand name and Arabic menu language, the flavour set is a moat that costs nothing to build and is genuinely awkward to copy — a competitor copying fig-and-apricot is visibly copying SHABIM, whereas a competitor copying mango is just importing.

WHAT IS *NOT* A MOAT, AND SHOULD NOT BE CLAIMED ON A SLIDE: the shape itself. The moulds are on Amazon; the trend is already in Costco and 7-Eleven; the Qatari incumbent went cloud-kitchen-to-Carrefour in twelve months. Shape buys attention, not defence. Defence is (1) mould quality, (2) the airbrushed hand, (3) cold chain, (4) fruit contracts, (5) the flavour set, (6) owning the Arabic name of the category before anyone else does — «بوبس» is already the word Gulf TikTok uses, and it is nobody's trademark.
